concepts.title: Temperature, Heat and Their Measurement
concepts.definition: Temperature grades the hotness of a body and heat is the energy that flows from hotter to colder bodies on contact. Thermometers use fixed reference points -- ice and steam points -- with scales (Celsius, Fahrenheit and the absolute Kelvin scale) related by fixed conversion rules; the Kelvin scale starts at absolute zero where molecular motion bottoms out.
concepts.key_idea: Heat is energy in transit; temperature is the level that decides the direction of that transit.
concepts.textbook_ref: keph203.txt lines 30-140 (sections 10.1, 10.2 temperature and heat, 10.3 measurement of temperature, thermometer scales and conversions)

solution_steps.explain: Temperature labels the hotness; heat measures the energy transferred because of a temperature difference.
Freezing and boiling water fix 0 and 100 in Celsius, 32 and 212 in Fahrenheit, 273.15 and 373.15 in kelvin.
The three scales are linearly related, so a shift-and-scale conversion moves between them exactly.

concepts.title: Thermal Expansion of Solids
concepts.definition: Heated bodies expand because stronger molecular vibration widens the average spacing. A solid grows in length by a coefficient of linear expansion times its length times the temperature rise, and its area and volume expansions follow with roughly double and triple that coefficient.
concepts.key_idea: One material number per substance -- multiply it by length and temperature rise to get the stretch.

concepts.title: Specific Heat Capacity and Calorimetry
concepts.definition: The heat needed to raise a body's temperature is its mass times its specific heat capacity times the rise. Calorimetry exploits this with the mixing principle: in an isolated calorimeter, heat lost by hot bodies equals heat gained by cold ones, which lets one measure specific heats and latent heats.
concepts.key_idea: Heat in equals mass times specific heat times rise -- and in a calorimeter losses balance gains.
concepts.textbook_ref: keph203.txt lines 321-430 (sections 10.6 specific heat capacity, 10.7 calorimetry, principle of calorimetry, heat equation Q = m c delta T)

solution_steps.explain: The heat capacity c times mass times the temperature rise gives the heat absorbed.

concepts.title: Change of State and Latent Heat
concepts.definition: During melting or boiling the temperature holds fixed while heat still flows in -- that heat goes into breaking bonds, not into heating. The required energy per unit mass is the latent heat of fusion (for melting) or of vaporisation (for boiling), enormous for water, which is why steam scalds and ice cools.
concepts.key_idea: Latent heat buys the change of state at constant temperature -- no thermometer movement until the phase change finishes.
concepts.textbook_ref: keph203.txt lines 431-540 (section 10.8 change of state, latent heat of fusion and vaporisation, melting point and boiling point pressure effects)

solution_steps.explain: Each kilogram changing state absorbs (or releases) the latent heat of the transition.

concepts.title: Heat Transfer: Conduction and Newton's Law of Cooling
concepts.definition: Heat travels by conduction through still materials at a rate set by the thermal conductivity, the area, the temperature difference and inversely by the thickness. For small excess temperatures a hot body also cools to its surroundings at a rate proportional to that temperature difference -- Newton's law of cooling.
concepts.key_idea: Conduction is a per-second energy flow through the material wall; cooling of a body in air follows a proportional decay.
concepts.textbook_ref: keph203.txt lines 541-680 (sections 10.9 heat transfer, conduction, thermal conductivity, 10.10 Newton's law of cooling, convection and radiation mention)

solution_steps.explain: Conductivity times area times temperature difference gathers the driving terms.
Thicker walls throttle the flow; the quotient is joules per second conducted.
